references.text: The priest shall take some of the blood and put it on the horns of the altar for the fragrant incense that stands before the Lord's presence in the tent of meeting, and he shall pour out the rest of the bull's blood at the base of the burnt offering altar.
The same ritual of putting blood on the horns of the altar and pouring out the remainder at its base describes the blood ritual for the sin offering.
The priest shall take some of the sin offering's blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar, and he shall pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
The priest shall take some of the blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar, the same blood ritual that Aaron performs.
Moses slaughtered the bull, took its blood, and put it with his finger on the horns of the altar all around. He purified the altar and poured out the blood at the base of the altar.
You shall take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and you shall pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

The Letter to the Hebrews explains that under the law almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness. This points to the significance of blood rituals in the Old Testament.
